```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "A supports a higher price point, $8–20/month anchored to Yoodli's published tiers, against B's $3.99–4.99/month. A higher price makes reaching paying customers within 90 days, and recovering the documented acquisition costs, more plausible for one person.",
    "A's demand evidence names a specific gap that a focused product could fill: the r/socialanxiety complaint that general chatbots won't give genuine negative feedback. B's demand evidence is either conditional on a UI rollback or comes from a builder describing their own frustration, not from a buyer.",
    "A has hints of payers beyond consumers that B lacks. The Cognity sells quote-based pricing to therapists and organizations, and Yoodli sells to enterprises. These give a solo founder possible B2B or clinician routes to a first payment. B is limited to App Store consumer subscriptions.",
    "B's case against is unusually strong and well sourced. Artifact had an 8-person team, millions in funding and a Google Play award, yet its downloads fell from 100K to about 12K per month and it shut down. Free absorption of the feature into Apple News, Google News and chatbots also squeezes the category. Nothing in A's brief is as damaging.",
    "Both categories are crowded with free and freemium players, so saturation does not separate them. A's risks are an undefined payer, efficacy skepticism from r/slp, and health-claim and privacy exposure. These can be worked around by choosing a non-clinical niche, such as phone-call or interview practice for anxious adults. B's core problem, low willingness to pay for general news, is structural."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's main willingness-to-pay evidence is one Syft Play Store review: \"Revert the UI back and I'll pay. Until then I'm deleting this and using inoreader.\" It is a single anecdote. The offer to pay depends on a UI rollback, not on AI personalization. The reviewer is leaving for a non-AI RSS reader, which arguably shows the AI feature is not what they value. Relatedly, the case-for claim that Bulletin, KhanList, Content Bite and Syft are 'monetizing' as single-developer apps has no revenue or subscriber data behind it. KhanList is listed with no IAP at all.",
  "confidence_note": "Low-to-moderate confidence. Neither brief shows anyone actually paying for a new entrant. A's payer is explicitly undefined, and its best testimonial comes from a competitor's own marketing page, so it is self-selected. A's ASO figure of $20–50 per user also sits oddly against its ~$3.76 ad CPA. A wins mainly because its pricing headroom is higher and it has no failure as decisive as Artifact. It does not win because its own evidence is strong."
}
```
